channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Gathers strength above 1.3350, but stays capped below 100-day average
item.description: The GBP/USD pair trades in positive territory around 1.3360 during the early European session on Friday. The British Pound (GBP) gathers strength against the US Dollar (USD) on a weaker-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices rose in India on Friday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Trades cautiously higher near mid-1.1400s amid mixed setup
item.description: The EUR/USD pair attracts some dip-buyers during the Asian session on Friday, stalling the previous day's modest pullback from the 1.1470-1.1475 region, or a nearly two-week high.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Holds gains near 112.00, but bearish bias persists below key moving averages
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross trades in positive territory around 111.75 during the early European trading hours on Friday. The Australian Dollar (AUD) strengthens against the Japanese Yen (JPY) following the Chinese economic data.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah declines as May's trade deficit suggests economic concerns
item.description: USD/IDR gains ground after registering minor losses in the previous day, trading around 18,000 during the Asian hours on Friday. The pair appreciates as the US Dollar (USD) holds its position despite a disappointing set of domestic labor data released on Thursday.

item.title: Gold advances to $4,200 neighborhood as reduced Fed hike bets keep USD depressed
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) is seen building on this week's recovery move from its lowest level since November 2025 and gaining positive traction for the third straight day on Friday.

item.title: United States Dollar Index faces pressure as traders reconsider hawkish Fed bets
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which gauges the Greenback’s value against six major currencies, is marginally down to near 100.80 during the Asian trading session on Friday.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD rises above $62.50 as Fed rate hike bets ease
item.description: XAG/USD gains ground for the fourth consecutive day, trading around $62.60 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Friday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar remains firm above 0.5700 after Chinese services PMI data
item.description: The NZD/USD pair gathers strength to around 0.5705 during the Asian trading hours on Friday. The New Zealand (NZD) remains strong following the Chinese economic data. The US markets will be closed on Friday in observance of Independence Day.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains on the front foot vs weaker USD after China Services PMI
item.description: The AUD/USD pair turns positive for the second straight day following a modest Asian session downtick to the 0.6910 region amid the emergence of fresh US Dollar (USD) selling.

item.title: China’s RatingDog Services PMI eases in June: What 54.1 means for Australian Dollar
item.description: China's Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) declined to 54.1 in June from 54.4 in May, the latest data published by RatingDog showed on Friday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar declines on falling oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD inches higher after registering modest losses in the previous day, trading around 1.4190 during the Asian hours on Friday. The currency pair is holding its ground as a tug-of-war unfolds between a weakening crude oil market and soft economic data out of the United States (US).

item.title: Japanese Yen reverses modest Asian session losses against USD as intervention risks loom
item.description: The USD/JPY pair attracts fresh sellers following a modest Asian session uptick to the 161.50 region and turns lower for the second straight day on Friday.

item.title: Japan's Katayama: Ready to act appropriately on currency fluctuations
item.description: Japan’s Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday that officials are ready to act appropriately on currency fluctuations. However, Katayama decllined to comment on specific currency levels.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.8047 vs. 6.8088 previous
item.description: On Friday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.8047 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.8088 and 6.7808 Reuters estimate.

item.title: British Pound strengthens to near 1.3350 as cooling US labor market weighs US Dollar
item.description: The GBP/USD pair trades with mild gains near 1.3350 during the early Asian trading hours on Friday. The US Dollar (USD) edges lower against the British Pound (GBP) on a weaker-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report. The US markets will be closed on Friday in observance of Independence Day.

item.title: WTI remains below $68.50 amid easing Middle East tensions
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price inches lower after registering modest gains in the previous day, trading around $68.40 during the Asian hours on Friday. The global energy market is experiencing a notable cooling period as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East begin to ease.

item.title: Euro softens below 1.1450 as softer Eurozone inflation trims ECB hike bets
item.description: The EUR/USD pair declines to around 1.1420 during the early Asian session on Thursday, pressured by a soft Eurozone inflation outlook. The US Dollar (USD) strengthens against the Euro (EUR) despite disappointing US June labor data.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Range trading after weakness fades against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang reports USD/CNH is consolidating after a prior decline to 6.7865, with prices oscillating between 6.7911 and 6.8025 and closing at 6.7948. He expects intraday action to remain confined to 6.7860–6.7990.

item.title: Iran vows “decisive response” to any US “miscalculation”
item.description: Iran’s joint military command warned any US interference in the Strait of Hormuz will be met with a “decisive and swift response” as tensions continue to roil negotiations, Aljazeera news agency reported on Thursday.

item.title: Australian Dollar back above the growth line, still just a passenger
item.description: Thursday belonged to the US Dollar, not the Aussie. A soft American payrolls print sent AUD/USD spiking toward 0.6950 on release, before it gave most of that back to close well off its high.

item.title: Gold gains momentum above $4,100 after weak US NFP data
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) gains traction to around $4,125 during the early Asian session on Friday. The precious metal extends the rally after weaker-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls ‌(NFP) data reduced expectations of Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hikes this year.

item.title: South Korean Won: Export strength fails to stop gains – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale reports that the Korean Won remains under selling pressure despite strong export growth and a wider trade surplus. USD/KRW has broken above the 1,550 psychological level, with interim resistance identified higher.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Renminbi gains weaken undervaluation claims – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu argues that current CNY strength has strategic value as China boosts imports of semiconductors from Japan, South Korea and Taiwan. He notes that renminbi gains versus NA-3 (JPY, KRW ve TWD), USD and EUR weaken any U.S./EU case on Chinese currency undervaluation.

item.title: Mexican Peso rises on soft US jobs data, intervention speculation
item.description: The Mexican Peso advanced, boosted by a weaker-than-expected US jobs report that weighed on the US Dollar, which was also undermined by a rumored intervention in FX markets by Japanese authorities. At the time of writing, the USD/MXN trades at 17.48, down 0.43%.

item.title: Thai Baht: External cushion less generous – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Global Economics & Markets Research highlights that Thailand’s external buffers remain credible, but current-account dynamics have turned less favorable. Apr–May deficits reflect strong imports of energy and capital goods alongside resilient exports, reducing domestic value-added.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar rises as softer US jobs data weighs on the US Dollar
item.description: The NZD/USD pair advanced toward the 0.5700 level on Thursday as the US Dollar (USD) weakened following softer-than-expected United States (US) employment data.

item.title: Pound Sterling holds the line, on loan from a cracking Dollar
item.description: The Pound bounced off the long-term support line that has repeatedly held near its seven-month lows, clawing back toward the cluster of moving averages overhead.

item.title: Japanese Yen bounces as Tokyo stops telegraphing its punches
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) rebounded from four-decade lows on Thursday, a move that owed nothing to the Bank of Japan (BoJ).

item.title: South Korean Won: Semiconductor risk and inflation dynamics – BNY
item.description: BNY’s report underscores heavy selling in South Korean semiconductor stocks and warns, via the OECD’s 2026 survey, that Korea’s reliance on chip exports heightens exposure to global tech-cycle swings.
